open_obligations.what_is_open: Construct a child oracle that discovers every coefficient-tuple fiber exactly once with additive subset-state and output cost, or formalize an oracle model and prove a matching lower bound.
open_obligations.obstruction: The fiber lemma canonicalizes inducing orders only after a tuple is known. A removed-set state can be an ideal of many different output support posets, while coefficient equality is determined by completed regression rows rather than by a frozen local edge color. Scanning every ideal for every output costs a product of the subset-state and output counts, and traversing all paths can still be factorial when there is only one output.
open_obligations.attempted: Canonical lexicographic paths, adjacent commuting-swap reduction, hashing completed paths, and reverse search were examined. Lexicographic minimality is only decidable after future parent coefficients are exposed; hashing retains factorial traversal; and reverse search lacks a polynomial-time inverse-child generator for branches accessible only through noncanonical inducing orders. No impossibility theorem is justified because the frozen handle does not specify a sufficiently formal query-oracle model.
open_obligations.partial_result: For every \(T\in\Theta_S(\mathcal O_S)\), the complete fiber of compatible inducing orders is exactly the set of linear extensions of \(G_T\). Thus factorial duplication inside a known fiber can be collapsed: the lexicographically least inducing order is obtained by greedy topological sorting, all inducing orders are connected by adjacent incomparable swaps, and \(\Gamma_\pi\succ0\) is then computed in polynomial time. This does not yet enumerate the previously unknown fibers with additive \(2^p+N_{\mathrm{out}}\) work.

prose_updates.tldr: On the restrictive component-aligned Gaussian LiMVAM class, the main completion result extends calibration subsets to an arbitrary observed view graph. A candidate common order is compatible exactly when every observed residual cross-block is diagonal and, separately for each variable, the resulting partial disturbance covariance has a positive-definite completion. For chordal view graphs this is the constructive maximal-clique test from the classical positive-definite matrix-completion theorem; a signed four-cycle shows that positive-definite edge blocks alone do not suffice for nonchordal graphs. The earlier calibration-subset certificate is the clique-plus-isolated-vertices special case. Independently, a sharp generic elbow proves that no paired block is insufficient while any one preassigned view pair identifies the full coefficient tuple off one proper algebraic exceptional set. Removed-set recursion and covariance-region inversion remain supporting results, with the latter requiring positive definiteness of the selected joint covariance. Exact-once output-sensitive quotient enumeration is not delivered and remains the explicit residual open question.

project_justification.gap: Existing multi-view LiMVAM identification results address full pairing under conditions on disturbance diversity, while Gaussian-DAG estimators target a point-identified DAG from one joint law. Neither line characterizes compatibility when cross-view covariances are observed on an arbitrary graph, where diagonal residual restrictions and positive-definite completion are distinct requirements. Existing enumeration results also do not supply the missing child oracle needed to quotient globally equal numerical coefficient tuples directly from the removed-set DAG.
project_justification.niche: For the component-aligned Gaussian subclass, a fixed candidate order determines every view-specific coefficient matrix from its marginal covariance. Each observed view edge then fixes entries of the coordinatewise disturbance covariance, so global compatibility becomes a positive-definite partial-matrix completion problem after the observable residual-diagonality test. This separates order testing, global noise feasibility, and coefficient recovery, and it retains every unpaired view marginal for coefficient estimation.
project_justification.fill: The graph-completion theorem proves necessity by restricting any full coordinatewise disturbance covariance to its observed diagonal and edge entries, and proves sufficiency by choosing one positive-definite completion for each variable and assembling independent Gaussian disturbance stacks. On chordal view graphs, the classical completion theorem reduces feasibility to positive definiteness of every maximal specified clique and supplies a constructive certificate. A nonchordal four-cycle with unit diagonals and successive edge correlations \(0.9,0.9,0.9,-0.9\) has positive-definite edge blocks but no positive-semidefinite completion, so edgewise checks alone are not valid in general. The generic calibration elbow separately proves that one observed pair is generically necessary and sufficient. The memoized removed-set DAG solves compatibility, but duplicate-free output-sensitive enumeration of all unknown tuple fibers remains open.

sampling_model.design: At population level, an observed view graph records exactly those paired cross-covariance blocks available in addition to every view marginal. The finite-sample inversion theorem specializes to the original calibration-plus-marginals design: one aligned calibration sample supplies joint observations for every view in \(S\), while each view may contribute additional same-population marginal observations.
sampling_model.overlap: The arbitrary-graph population theorem requires alignment only for each observed view edge. The finite-sample guarantee is proved for the clique of blocks generated by a jointly aligned subset \(S\). No unobserved cross-view block is used, and signal-dependent selection, population transport, and source-specific target laws are excluded.

prose_updates.related_work: HeurtebiseEtAl2026LiMVAM is the flagship model anchor: its Section 4.6 uses edgewise cross-view correlation diversity to identify a partial order and view-specific coefficients under full pairing. The present conclusions are only for the narrower component-aligned Gaussian subclass and do not claim containment of the published Heurtebise class. ShimizuEtAl2011DirectLiNGAM and Shimizu2012JointLiNGAM motivate recursive residualization under non-Gaussianity, but they do not prove removed-set path independence or partial-view-graph covariance completion. ChenEtAl2024IndividualCausal and GhassamiEtAl2018MultiDomain pool population or domain information through ICA structure or heterogeneity rather than through selected paired cross-covariance blocks. HyttinenEberhardtHoyer2012Overlapping studies overlapping experimental total-effect measurements, not residual covariance restrictions among passive views. The positive-definite completion theorem of Grone, Johnson, S\'a, and Wolkowicz (1984, Theorem 7) supplies the chordal maximal-clique criterion used by the graph specialization; the arbitrary-graph reduction and the signed four-cycle obstruction are derived for the present disturbance matrices. GuoPerkovic2021MinimalEffects partitions graphical classes by total-effect signatures, WienobstEtAl2023MECEnumeration enumerates graph-distinct Markov-equivalent DAGs, WangEtAl2023EquivalenceEnumeration treats locally colored decomposable AND--OR graphs, and AvisFukuda1996ReverseSearch requires a locally searchable parent relation. None establishes the missing quotient child oracle for global numerical modified-Cholesky tuples, so \(\text{oeq:output-sensitive-quotient}\) remains open. HauserBuhlmann2014ActiveLearning and LindgrenEtAl2018CostAware concern intervention-target design through separating systems, whereas the present calibration choice is passive observation of view-pair covariance blocks. GhoshalHonorio2018LinearSEM uses recursive Schur updates and score gaps in a point-identifying linear SEM. GaoTaiAragam2022GaussianDAG studies point-identifying Gaussian-DAG estimation rather than partial paired-view calibration and set-valued order compatibility. Vershynin2018HighDimensionalProbability supplies Gaussian singular-value concentration used for covariance radii, and ChernozhukovHongTamer2007SetInference supplies the general criterion-inversion comparison; neither gives the LiMVAM-specific residual and path-product moduli. MohanPearl2021MissingData studies recoverability under missingness graphs, whereas the present sourcewise-iid common-population sampling design assumes away selection and transport. TaylorEtAl2017CamCAN documents the MEG and MRI cohort that motivates a future diagnostic application, but it does not validate component alignment or the calibration-sampling assumptions.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The graph-completion characterization is population-level and remains confined to the component-aligned Gaussian subclass. For nonchordal view graphs, positive definiteness of every specified edge block is only necessary; global completion must still be checked. The generic elbow is relative to a fixed-order finite-dimensional parameterization and supplies no uniform distance from its algebraic exceptional set. Covariance-region inversion requires the selected joint covariance \(\Sigma^{SS}\succ0\) in addition to positive-definite view marginals; this premise is essential for whitening and excludes singular identical-view laws. Its Hausdorff and poset guarantees also require fixed feasibility and path-product margins. The \(2^p\)-state recursion counts exact-real arithmetic rather than bit complexity. Most importantly, \(\text{oeq:output-sensitive-quotient}\) remains unresolved: known-fiber canonicalization does not yield an exact-once algorithm with additive \(2^p+N_{\mathrm{out}}\) cost, and no hardness claim is justified without a formal oracle model.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The arbitrary-view-graph completion theorem, its chordal specialization, the nonchordal obstruction, the generic calibration elbow, fixed-order recovery, removed-set recursion, essential poset, and covariance-region inversion concern only the component-aligned Gaussian subclass with positive-definite coordinate disturbance covariances. They do not transfer automatically to unrestricted LiMVAMs or establish the assumptions used by Heurtebise et al. Genericity is relative to coefficients respecting a fixed common order and gives no uniform identification margin. Finite-sample inversion additionally assumes a positive-definite selected joint covariance and sourcewise-iid common-population sampling; selection and transport are outside the model. Cam-CAN MEG and fMRI remain prospective diagnostic applications rather than empirical validation. Exact-once output-sensitive quotient enumeration remains open.

proofs.proof_tex:
Set \(K=K_{\mathrm{obs}}=m+1\) and
\[
t_\alpha=\sqrt{2\log(2K/\alpha)}.
\tag{1}
\]
We first prove simultaneous coverage. Consider one of the \(K\) covariance sources: either the aligned \(S\)-vector, with \((d,n,\Sigma_0)=(d_S,n_S,\Sigma^{SS})\), or the observations from view \(a\), with \((d,n,\Sigma_0)=(p,n_a,\Sigma^{aa})\). The selected case satisfies \(\Sigma_0\succ0\) by \(\text{ass:selected-joint-nondegeneracy}\). In every marginal case, \(\lambda_*>0\) and the definition of \(\lambda_*\) in \(\text{def:local-stability-modulus}\) give
\[
\lambda_{\min}(\Sigma^{aa})\ge\lambda_*>0,
\tag{2}
\]
so \(\Sigma_0\succ0\) there as well. Let \(Y\) be the \(n\times d\) data matrix whose rows are the sampled vectors transposed, and define
\[
G=Y\Sigma_0^{-1/2}.
\tag{3}
\]
The inverse square root in (3) exists in the selected case precisely because of \(\text{ass:selected-joint-nondegeneracy}\), and in the marginal cases by (2). By \(\text{ass:centered-gaussian-law}\), each row of \(G\) is centered Gaussian with identity covariance, hence has independent standard normal coordinates. By \(\text{ass:calibration-sampling}\) for the selected source and \(\text{ass:marginal-sampling}\) for a marginal source, the rows are independent and identically distributed. Thus all entries of \(G\) are independent standard normal variables.

For this source put
\[
\eta=\sqrt{d/n}+t_\alpha/\sqrt n.
\tag{4}
\]
The assumed inequality \(\eta<1\) implies \(n>d\), and in particular \(n\ge d\), so \(\text{lem:gaussian-extreme-singular-values}\) applies with \(t=t_\alpha\). Since \(2\exp(-t_\alpha^2/2)=\alpha/K\), with probability at least \(1-\alpha/K\),
\[
1-\eta\le s_{\min}(G)/\sqrt n
\le s_{\max}(G)/\sqrt n\le1+\eta.
\tag{5}
\]
Set \(\ell=(1-\eta)^2\) and \(v=(1+\eta)^2\). The empirical covariance is
\[
\widehat\Sigma
=\frac1nY^{\mathsf T}Y
=\Sigma_0^{1/2}\frac{G^{\mathsf T}G}{n}\Sigma_0^{1/2}.
\tag{6}
\]
Squaring (5) and applying the congruence in (6) yields
\[
\ell\Sigma_0\preceq\widehat\Sigma\preceq v\Sigma_0.
\tag{7}
\]
Because \(\eta<1\), \(\ell>0\). Hence (7) implies
\[
\Sigma_0\preceq\ell^{-1}\widehat\Sigma,
\qquad
\Sigma_0\succeq v^{-1}\widehat\Sigma.
\tag{8}
\]
If \(c=\ell^{-1}-1\), then \(1-v^{-1}\le c\), and (8) gives
\[
-c\widehat\Sigma
\preceq \Sigma_0-\widehat\Sigma
\preceq c\widehat\Sigma.
\tag{9}
\]
Taking Rayleigh quotients in (9) proves
\[
\|\Sigma_0-\widehat\Sigma\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\le\bigl((1-\eta)^{-2}-1\bigr)
\|\widehat\Sigma\|_{\mathrm{op}}.
\tag{10}
\]

For the selected source, (4) and (10) are exactly the radius \(r_{S,n}(\alpha)\); for view \(a\), they are exactly \(r_{a,n}(\alpha)\), by \(\text{def:covariance-region}\). A union bound over the \(K=m+1\) sources gives a joint event \(\mathcal E_n(\alpha)\) satisfying
\[
\Pr\{\mathcal E_n(\alpha)\}\ge1-K(\alpha/K)=1-\alpha.
\tag{11}
\]
No independence among the \(K\) covariance estimators is used in (11). On \(\mathcal E_n(\alpha)\), all inequalities defining \(\mathcal C_n(\alpha)\) hold for \(\mathcal O_S\). Its selected joint covariance is positive definite by \(\text{ass:selected-joint-nondegeneracy}\), and all its marginal covariances are positive definite by (2). Therefore
\[
\mathcal O_S\in\mathcal C_n(\alpha)
\quad\text{and}\quad
\Pr\{\mathcal O_S\in\mathcal C_n(\alpha)\}\ge1-\alpha.
\tag{12}
\]
By the union in \(\text{def:region-inversion}\), (12) also gives
\[
\Theta_S(\mathcal O_S)
\subseteq\widehat\Theta_{S,n}(\alpha)
\quad\text{on }\mathcal E_n(\alpha).
\tag{13}
\]

We next establish the deterministic perturbation bounds. Fix a positive-definite \(\mathcal O'_S\), put
\[
u=d_{\mathrm{obs}}(\mathcal O_S,\mathcal O'_S)
\le\min\{\lambda_*/2,L_B^{-1}\},
\tag{14}
\]
and fix an order \(\pi\), a view \(a\), a row label \(j\), and its predecessor set \(P\) under \(\pi\). The row is zero when \(P=\varnothing\), so suppose \(P\ne\varnothing\). In the notation of \(\text{def:modified-cholesky}\), write
\[
\beta=\Sigma^{aa}[j,P]\Sigma^{aa}[P,P]^{-1},
\qquad
\beta'=\Sigma'^{aa}[j,P]\Sigma'^{aa}[P,P]^{-1}.
\tag{15}
\]
Compression by coordinate-selection matrices does not increase operator norm. Consequently every covariance block in (15) changes by at most \(u\). For every unit vector \(x\), (2) and (14) imply
\[
x^{\mathsf T}\Sigma'^{aa}[P,P]x
\ge x^{\mathsf T}\Sigma^{aa}[P,P]x-u
\ge\lambda_*-u
\ge\lambda_*/2.
\tag{16}
\]
Thus
\[
\|\Sigma'^{aa}[P,P]^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le2/\lambda_*.
\tag{17}
\]
The resolvent identity and (17) give
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\|\Sigma'^{aa}[P,P]^{-1}-\Sigma^{aa}[P,P]^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\\
&\qquad\le
\|\Sigma'^{aa}[P,P]^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\|\Sigma'^{aa}[P,P]-\Sigma^{aa}[P,P]\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\|\Sigma^{aa}[P,P]^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\le\frac{2u}{\lambda_*^2}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{18}
\]
Since \(\|\Sigma^{aa}[j,P]\|_2\le\|\Sigma^{aa}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le K_*\), subtracting (15), adding and subtracting \(\Sigma^{aa}[j,P]\Sigma'^{aa}[P,P]^{-1}\), and using (17)--(18) yields
\[
\|\beta'-\beta\|_2
\le\frac{2u}{\lambda_*}+\frac{2K_*u}{\lambda_*^2}
=2u(\lambda_*^{-1}+K_*\lambda_*^{-2}).
\tag{19}
\]
There are at most \(p\) rows. The operator norm is bounded by the Frobenius norm, so (19) and the definition of \(L_B\) in \(\text{def:local-stability-modulus}\) imply
\[
\|B_\pi^{(a)}(\mathcal O'_S)-B_\pi^{(a)}(\mathcal O_S)\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\le L_Bu.
\tag{20}
\]

Moreover, (14), (16), and \(\|\Sigma'^{aa}[j,P]\|_2\le K_*+u\) give
\[
\|\beta'\|_2
\le\frac{2(K_*+u)}{\lambda_*}
\le1+\frac{2K_*}{\lambda_*}.
\tag{21}
\]
The same upper bound also applies to \(\beta\). Hence, using \(L_\pi^{(a)}=I_p-B_\pi^{(a)}\), both the population and perturbed residualizers satisfy
\[
\|L_\pi^{(a)}\|_{\mathrm{op}},
\|L_\pi'{}^{(a)}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\le1+\sqrt p\left(1+\frac{2K_*}{\lambda_*}\right)
=G_*.
\tag{22}
\]
For an observed pair \((a,b)\), abbreviate the population residualizers by \(L_a,L_b\) and the perturbed residualizers by \(L'_a,L'_b\). From \(\text{def:residual-cross-blocks}\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
R_\pi'{}^{ab}-R_\pi^{ab}
={}&L'_a(\Sigma'^{ab}-\Sigma^{ab})L_b'{}^{\mathsf T}
+(L'_a-L_a)\Sigma^{ab}L_b'{}^{\mathsf T}\\
&+L_a\Sigma^{ab}(L'_b-L_b)^{\mathsf T}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{23}
\]
By (20), (22), the definition of \(K_*\), and submultiplicativity,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\|R_\pi'{}^{ab}-R_\pi^{ab}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
&\le\{G_*^2+2L_BG_*K_*\}u\\
&\le\{G_*^2+L_BG_*(2K_*+\lambda_*/2)\}u\\
&=L_Ru=\omega_{\mathrm{feas}}(u).
\end{aligned}
\tag{24}
\]

For an ordered vertex pair \(e=(v,w)\), define
\[
w_e(T)=\max_{a\in M}|B_{wv}^{(a)}|.
\tag{25}
\]
Equation (20) implies \(|w_e(T')-w_e(T)|\le L_Bu\). Population weights are at most \(K_B\); by (14), perturbed weights are at most \(K_B+1\). If \(g=(v_0,\ldots,v_\ell)\) is a directed path for the fixed order, then \(1\le\ell\le p-1\). A telescoping product expansion therefore gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\left|
\prod_{h=1}^{\ell}w_{(v_{h-1},v_h)}(T')
-\prod_{h=1}^{\ell}w_{(v_{h-1},v_h)}(T)
\right|\\
&\qquad\le \ell(K_B+1)^{\ell-1}L_Bu
\le(p-1)(K_B+1)^{p-2}L_Bu\\
&\qquad=L_{\mathrm{path}}L_Bu
=\omega_{\mathrm{path}}(u).
\end{aligned}
\tag{26}
\]

Now suppose \(\pi\notin\Pi_S(\mathcal O_S)\). By \(\text{ass:feasibility-separation}\) and \(\text{def:feasibility-margin}\), some distinct \(a,b\in S\) and some off-diagonal coordinate of \(R_\pi^{ab}\) have absolute value at least \(\kappa_{\mathrm{feas}}\). Each entrywise change is at most the operator-norm change in (24). Consequently, if \(\omega_{\mathrm{feas}}(u)\le\kappa_{\mathrm{feas}}/2\), the same coordinate of \(R_\pi'{}^{ab}\) has absolute value at least \(\kappa_{\mathrm{feas}}/2>0\). The compatibility definition then excludes \(\pi\) at \(\mathcal O'_S\). Since this applies to every population-incompatible order,
\[
\Pi_S(\mathcal O'_S)\subseteq\Pi_S(\mathcal O_S).
\tag{27}
\]

Return to the coverage event \(\mathcal E_n(\alpha)\). If \(\mathcal O'_S\in\mathcal C_n(\alpha)\), then \(\mathcal O_S\) and \(\mathcal O'_S\) are each within the corresponding radius of the same empirical block. Every selected cross-block is a compression of the selected joint block. The triangle inequality and the definition of \(\bar r_n(\alpha)\) therefore yield
\[
d_{\mathrm{obs}}(\mathcal O_S,\mathcal O'_S)
\le2\bar r_n(\alpha).
\tag{28}
\]
Assume the three small-radius inequalities displayed in the theorem. For every \(T'\in\widehat\Theta_{S,n}(\alpha)\), \(\text{def:region-inversion}\) and \(\text{def:identified-tuple-set}\) provide \(\mathcal O'_S\in\mathcal C_n(\alpha)\) and \(\pi\in\Pi_S(\mathcal O'_S)\) such that
\[
T'=T_\pi(\mathcal O'_S).
\tag{29}
\]
Equations (27)--(28) give \(\pi\in\Pi_S(\mathcal O_S)\), while (20) gives
\[
d_{\mathrm{coef}}\bigl(T',T_\pi(\mathcal O_S)\bigr)
\le2L_B\bar r_n(\alpha).
\tag{30}
\]
Conversely, (13) puts every element of \(\Theta_S(\mathcal O_S)\) in \(\widehat\Theta_{S,n}(\alpha)\). Thus both directed Hausdorff distances are controlled, and
\[
d_{\mathrm H}^{d_{\mathrm{coef}}}
\bigl(\widehat\Theta_{S,n}(\alpha),\Theta_S(\mathcal O_S)\bigr)
\le2L_B\bar r_n(\alpha).
\tag{31}
\]

It remains to identify the essential relation. Inclusion (13) immediately gives
\[
\widehat\prec_{S,n}(\alpha)\subseteq\prec_S,
\tag{32}
\]
because a relation common to the larger estimated tuple set is common to its population subset. Conversely, fix \(i\prec_S j\) and any \(T'\) as in (29). Its counterpart \(T=T_\pi(\mathcal O_S)\) belongs to \(\Theta_S(\mathcal O_S)\) by (27). By \(\text{ass:path-product-separation}\) and \(\text{def:path-margin}\), an \(i\)-to-\(j\) path in \(G_T\) has weight product at least \(\kappa_{\mathrm{path}}\). Equation (26) and the third small-radius inequality leave the same path product in \(T'\) at least \(\kappa_{\mathrm{path}}/2>0\). Every factor is therefore positive, so every edge of that path occurs in the union support graph \(G_{T'}\). Thus \(i\widehat\prec_{S,n}(\alpha)j\). Combined with (32) and \(\text{def:essential-poset}\), this proves
\[
\widehat\prec_{S,n}(\alpha)=\prec_S.
\tag{33}
\]

Finally take \(\alpha=\alpha_n\). By the stated vanishing-radii condition, \(\bar r_n(\alpha_n)\to0\) in probability and the radii are eventually defined with probability tending to one. Since \(\lambda_*,L_B,L_R,L_{\mathrm{path}},\kappa_{\mathrm{feas}},\kappa_{\mathrm{path}}\) are fixed positive population quantities, the three small-radius inequalities hold on an event \(\mathcal H_n\) with \(\Pr(\mathcal H_n)\to1\). Equation (11) and \(\alpha_n\to0\) give
\[
\Pr\{\mathcal E_n(\alpha_n)\cap\mathcal H_n\}
\ge1-\alpha_n-\Pr(\mathcal H_n^{\mathsf c})\longrightarrow1.
\tag{34}
\]
On this intersection, (31) is bounded by \(2L_B\bar r_n(\alpha_n)=o_P(1)\), and (33) holds exactly. Therefore the coefficient sets converge in Hausdorff distance in probability and the essential poset is recovered exactly with probability tending to one.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: Suppose \(\Sigma^{SS}\succ0\). Under the centered Gaussian law and the calibration and marginal sampling conditions, whenever \(\eta_{S,n}<1\) and every \(\eta_{a,n}<1\), the explicit radii in \(\mathcal C_n(\alpha)\) satisfy \(\Pr\{\mathcal O_S\in\mathcal C_n(\alpha)\}\ge1-\alpha\), and on this event \(\Theta_S(\mathcal O_S)\subseteq\widehat\Theta_{S,n}(\alpha)\). More explicitly, for any positive-definite \(\mathcal O'_S\) with \(u=d_{\mathrm{obs}}(\mathcal O_S,\mathcal O'_S)\le\min\{\lambda_*/2,L_B^{-1}\}\), every order and observed view pair obey \(\|B_\pi^{(a)}(\mathcal O'_S)-B_\pi^{(a)}(\mathcal O_S)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le L_Bu\) and \(\|R_\pi^{ab}(\mathcal O'_S)-R_\pi^{ab}(\mathcal O_S)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\omega_{\mathrm{feas}}(u)=L_Ru\); every corresponding directed-path product changes by at most \(\omega_{\mathrm{path}}(u)=L_{\mathrm{path}}L_Bu\). Hence, if \(\omega_{\mathrm{feas}}(u)\le\kappa_{\mathrm{feas}}/2\), then \(\Pi_S(\mathcal O'_S)\subseteq\Pi_S(\mathcal O_S)\). On the coverage event, if \(2\bar r_n(\alpha)\le\min\{\lambda_*/2,L_B^{-1}\}\), \(\omega_{\mathrm{feas}}(2\bar r_n(\alpha))\le\kappa_{\mathrm{feas}}/2\), and \(\omega_{\mathrm{path}}(2\bar r_n(\alpha))\le\kappa_{\mathrm{path}}/2\), then the Hausdorff distance induced by \(d_{\mathrm{coef}}\) from \(\widehat\Theta_{S,n}(\alpha)\) to \(\Theta_S(\mathcal O_S)\) is at most \(2L_B\bar r_n(\alpha)\), and \(\widehat\prec_{S,n}(\alpha)=\prec_S\). Consequently, if \(\min(n_S,\min_{a\in M}n_a)\to\infty\), the two novel margins are bounded below by \(\kappa_{\mathrm{feas}}>0\) and \(\kappa_{\mathrm{path}}>0\), and \(\alpha_n\to0\) with vanishing radii, then Hausdorff consistency and exact essential-poset recovery hold in probability.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The current coverage claim permits a singular selected joint covariance even though the paired-sample proof requires its inverse square root and the confidence region requires the population selected joint block to be positive definite. The explicit premise excludes that boundary case without changing the identification, stability, or limit conclusions.

proposed_assumptions.reason: The selected Gaussian sample can be whitened and the population observed moment collection can belong to the positive-definite covariance region only when its selected joint covariance is positive definite.
proposed_assumptions.not_crux: This is a nondegeneracy condition required only for whitening the selected Gaussian sample and for eligibility of the population covariance in the positive-definite confidence region; it does not imply compatibility, coefficient identification, coverage, or poset recovery.

proposed.statement: Suppose \(\Sigma^{SS}\succ0\). Under the centered Gaussian law and the calibration and marginal sampling conditions, whenever \(\eta_{S,n}<1\) and every \(\eta_{a,n}<1\), the explicit radii in \(\mathcal C_n(\alpha)\) satisfy \(\Pr\{\mathcal O_S\in\mathcal C_n(\alpha)\}\ge1-\alpha\), and on this event \(\Theta_S(\mathcal O_S)\subseteq\widehat\Theta_{S,n}(\alpha)\). More explicitly, for any positive-definite \(\mathcal O'_S\) with \(u=d_{\mathrm{obs}}(\mathcal O_S,\mathcal O'_S)\le\min\{\lambda_*/2,L_B^{-1}\}\), every order and observed view pair obey \(\|B_\pi^{(a)}(\mathcal O'_S)-B_\pi^{(a)}(\mathcal O_S)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le L_Bu\) and \(\|R_\pi^{ab}(\mathcal O'_S)-R_\pi^{ab}(\mathcal O_S)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\omega_{\mathrm{feas}}(u)=L_Ru\); every corresponding directed-path product changes by at most \(\omega_{\mathrm{path}}(u)=L_{\mathrm{path}}L_Bu\). Hence, if \(\omega_{\mathrm{feas}}(u)\le\kappa_{\mathrm{feas}}/2\), then \(\Pi_S(\mathcal O'_S)\subseteq\Pi_S(\mathcal O_S)\). On the coverage event, if \(2\bar r_n(\alpha)\le\min\{\lambda_*/2,L_B^{-1}\}\), \(\omega_{\mathrm{feas}}(2\bar r_n(\alpha))\le\kappa_{\mathrm{feas}}/2\), and \(\omega_{\mathrm{path}}(2\bar r_n(\alpha))\le\kappa_{\mathrm{path}}/2\), then the Hausdorff distance induced by \(d_{\mathrm{coef}}\) from \(\widehat\Theta_{S,n}(\alpha)\) to \(\Theta_S(\mathcal O_S)\) is at most \(2L_B\bar r_n(\alpha)\), and \(\widehat\prec_{S,n}(\alpha)=\prec_S\). Consequently, if \(\min(n_S,\min_{a\in M}n_a)\to\infty\), the two novel margins are bounded below by \(\kappa_{\mathrm{feas}}>0\) and \(\kappa_{\mathrm{path}}>0\), and \(\alpha_n\to0\) with vanishing radii, then Hausdorff consistency and exact essential-poset recovery hold in probability.
proposed.justification: Set inversion makes uncertainty honest when the population output is non-singleton, while the explicit moduli translate covariance error into branch and ancestral-path stability.
proposed.gap: ChernozhukovHongTamer2007SetInference gives general contour inversion, while GhoshalHonorio2018LinearSEM uses precision-diagonal and nonzero-precision-entry gaps for one recursive graph. Neither source defines the wrong-order residual or common-ancestral path-product margins, nor derives the displayed LiMVAM covariance-to-margin moduli.
proposed.consumer: A future Cam-CAN MEG or fMRI diagnostic analysis can report an uncertainty-aware sensitivity envelope only after checking common-target sampling and failing to reject the component-aligned repeated-sensor mechanism on observed calibration blocks.

proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(\theta\in\Omega_{\pi_0}^{\mathrm{CA}}\), and write \(A^{(a)}=(I_p-B^{(a)})^{-1}\).  Strict lower triangularity in the order \(\pi_0\) makes \(B^{(a)}\) nilpotent, so
\[
(I_p-B^{(a)})^{-1}=\sum_{q=0}^{p-1}(B^{(a)})^q.
\tag{1}
\]
Moreover, \(\Gamma_i\succ0\) implies \(\Gamma_i[a,a]>0\).  The covariance formula in \(\text{def:fixed-order-open-parameter-space}\) therefore yields
\[
\Sigma_\theta^{aa}
=A^{(a)}\operatorname{diag}_{i\in V}(\Gamma_i[a,a])(A^{(a)})^{\mathsf T}
\succ0.
\tag{2}
\]
Thus every principal submatrix inverted in \(\text{def:modified-cholesky}\) is positive definite and has positive determinant.

Equation (1) shows that every entry of \(\Sigma_\theta^{ab}\) is polynomial in the free coordinates of \(\theta\).  Applying
\(C^{-1}=\operatorname{adj}(C)/\det(C)\) to each predecessor covariance in \(\text{def:modified-cholesky}\) shows that every entry of \(B_\pi^{(a)}\), and consequently every entry of
\[
R_\pi^{ab}=(I_p-B_\pi^{(a)})\Sigma_\theta^{ab}
(I_p-B_\pi^{(b)})^{\mathsf T},
\tag{3}
\]
is rational with a denominator that is a product of the positive principal minors from (2).  Hence the denominator clearing in \(\text{def:pairwise-exceptional-variety}\) preserves whether an entry is zero.

Fix \(1\le a<b\le m\) and \(\pi\ne\pi_0\).  Two distinct total orders have a discordant pair, so there are \(u,v\in V\) such that \(u\) precedes \(v\) under \(\pi_0\), whereas \(v\) precedes \(u\) under \(\pi\).  Consider \(\theta_\pi^{ab}\) from \(\text{def:wrong-order-nonvanishing-witness}\).  For \(w\in\{u,v\}\), the covariance \(\Gamma_w\), after a simultaneous permutation of view coordinates, is the direct sum of
\[
\begin{pmatrix}1&r_w\\ r_w&1\end{pmatrix}
\quad\text{and}\quad I_{m-2}.
\]
Its eigenvalues are \(1-r_w\), \(1+r_w\), and \(1\) with multiplicity \(m-2\), all positive because \(|r_w|<1\).  Every other \(\Gamma_i\) is \(I_m\), and the only nonzero coefficient, \(\beta\), respects \(\pi_0\).  Thus
\[
\theta_\pi^{ab}\in\Omega_{\pi_0}^{\mathrm{CA}}.
\tag{4}
\]

Variables outside \(\{u,v\}\) are uncorrelated with this two-variable subsystem and therefore do not change the following population regression coefficients when they occur in a predecessor set.  In views \(a\) and \(b\),
\[
X_u=\varepsilon_u,
\qquad
X_v=\beta\varepsilon_u+\varepsilon_v,
\qquad
\operatorname{Var}(\varepsilon_u)=\operatorname{Var}(\varepsilon_v)=1.
\tag{5}
\]
Since \(v\) precedes \(u\) under \(\pi\), the wrong-order innovations are
\[
\widetilde\varepsilon_v=X_v,
\qquad
\widetilde\varepsilon_u
=X_u-\frac{\operatorname{Cov}(X_u,X_v)}{\operatorname{Var}(X_v)}X_v
=X_u-\frac{\beta}{1+\beta^2}X_v.
\tag{6}
\]
Using cross-variable disturbance orthogonality and the witness covariances in (6) gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Cov}\!\left(\widetilde\varepsilon_u^{(a)},
\widetilde\varepsilon_v^{(b)}\right)
&=\operatorname{Cov}\!\left(
\frac{\varepsilon_u^{(a)}-\beta\varepsilon_v^{(a)}}{1+\beta^2},
\beta\varepsilon_u^{(b)}+\varepsilon_v^{(b)}\right)\\
&=\frac{\beta}{1+\beta^2}(r_u-r_v)\ne0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{7}
\]
This is, up to transpose orientation, an off-diagonal entry of \(R_\pi^{ab}\).  Its cleared numerator is nonzero at \(\theta_\pi^{ab}\), so
\[
F_\pi^{ab}\not\equiv0.
\tag{8}
\]

There are finitely many unordered view pairs and wrong permutations.  A finite product of nonzero real polynomials is nonzero, since under any monomial order the leading coefficient of the product is the product of the nonzero leading coefficients.  It follows from (8) that
\[
Q_{\mathrm{all}}\not\equiv0.
\tag{9}
\]
The set \(\Omega_{\pi_0}^{\mathrm{CA}}\) is nonempty and relatively open in its free Euclidean coordinates: the point having \(B^{(a)}=0\) and \(\Gamma_i=I_m\) belongs to it, and the positive-definite cone is open.  By \(\text{lem:nonzero-polynomial-null-set}\), (9) implies that \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{all},\pi_0}\) is proper, has empty relative interior, and has relative Lebesgue measure zero.  Any parameter law absolutely continuous with respect to that relative Lebesgue measure therefore assigns probability zero to this exceptional set.

We next identify the exact fixed-pair failure locus.  Fix \(a<b\).  Positivity of all denominator factors, the fact that a sum of real squares vanishes exactly when every summand vanishes, and (3) imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
F_\pi^{ab}(\theta)=0
&\Longleftrightarrow f_{\pi,ij}^{ab}(\theta)=0
\quad\text{for every }i\ne j\\
&\Longleftrightarrow \operatorname{offdiag}(R_\pi^{ab}(\theta))=0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{10}
\]
Also \(R_\pi^{ba}=(R_\pi^{ab})^{\mathsf T}\), because \(\Sigma^{ba}=(\Sigma^{ab})^{\mathsf T}\), so either orientation tests the unordered pair.  The true order \(\pi_0\) is compatible by \(\text{lem:fixed-order-residual-characterization}\).  Combining that fact, (10), and \(\text{def:pairwise-exceptional-variety}\) gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\theta\in\mathcal E_{ab,\pi_0}
&\Longleftrightarrow
F_\pi^{ab}(\theta)=0\quad\text{for at least one }\pi\ne\pi_0\\
&\Longleftrightarrow
\Pi_{\{a,b\}}(\mathcal O_{\{a,b\}})\ne\{\pi_0\}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{11}
\]

If \(\theta\notin\mathcal E_{\mathrm{all},\pi_0}\), every factor of \(Q_{\mathrm{all}}(\theta)\) is nonzero.  Applying (10) for every pair and every wrong order yields simultaneously
\[
\Pi_{\{a,b\}}(\mathcal O_{\{a,b\}})=\{\pi_0\}
\quad\text{for every }1\le a<b\le m.
\tag{12}
\]
The complete coefficient characterization in \(\text{lem:fixed-order-residual-characterization}\) then proves
\[
\Theta_{\{a,b\}}(\mathcal O_{\{a,b\}})=\{T_{\pi_0}\}.
\tag{13}
\]
Full calibration retains \(\pi_0\) and imposes every pair restriction, so its compatible-order set is contained in the compatible-order set for any one pair.  Equations (12)--(13) therefore give
\[
\Theta_M(\mathcal O_M)=\{T_{\pi_0}\}.
\tag{14}
\]
Thus (13)--(14) prove, rather than define, equality between the structural coefficient target and the observable residual-restriction functional.

If the pairwise coefficient set differs from \(\{T_{\pi_0}\}\), then its compatible-order set cannot be \(\{\pi_0\}\).  Hence the coefficient-nonidentification locus is contained in \(\mathcal E_{ab,\pi_0}\) by (11).  The containment can be strict.  Indeed, take \(B^{(a)}=0\) for every view and \(\Gamma_i=I_m\) for every coordinate.  Then \(\Sigma^{aa}=I_p\) and \(\Sigma^{ab}=0\) for \(a\ne b\).  For every \(\pi\), modified Cholesky gives \(B_\pi^{(a)}=0\) and \(R_\pi^{ab}=0\), whence
\[
\Pi_{\{a,b\}}(\mathcal O_{\{a,b\}})=\mathfrak S_V,
\qquad
\Theta_{\{a,b\}}(\mathcal O_{\{a,b\}})
=\{(0)_{a\in M}\}=\{T_{\pi_0}\}.
\tag{15}
\]
Because \(p\ge2\), a wrong order exists, so (15) lies in \(\mathcal E_{ab,\pi_0}\) but not in the coefficient-nonidentification locus.

It remains to prove the lower side of the calibration elbow.  Fix \(\pi\in\mathfrak S_V\) and \(a\in M\).  The rows of \(L_\pi^{(a)}X^{(a)}\) are successive least-squares innovations.  The normal equations make the innovation at position \(k\) orthogonal to the span of the variables at positions \(1,\ldots,k-1\), while every earlier innovation lies in that span.  Distinct innovations are therefore orthogonal, and
\[
D_\pi^{(a)}:=R_\pi^{aa}
=L_\pi^{(a)}\Sigma^{aa}(L_\pi^{(a)})^{\mathsf T}
\tag{16}
\]
is diagonal.  It is positive definite because \(\Sigma^{aa}\succ0\) and the unit order-triangular matrix \(L_\pi^{(a)}\) is invertible.  Hence every \(D_\pi^{(a)}[j,j]>0\).

For each \(j\in V\), define
\[
\Gamma_{\pi,j}^{\mathrm{marg}}
:=\operatorname{diag}_{a\in M}\bigl(D_\pi^{(a)}[j,j]\bigr)\succ0.
\tag{17}
\]
Let \((Z_j)_{j\in V}\) be independent standard Gaussian vectors in \(\mathbb R^m\), and put
\[
\widetilde\varepsilon_j
:=\operatorname{diag}_{a\in M}\!\left(\sqrt{D_\pi^{(a)}[j,j]}\right)Z_j,
\qquad
\widetilde X^{(a)}=(I_p-B_\pi^{(a)})^{-1}\widetilde\varepsilon^{(a)}.
\tag{18}
\]
This construction is jointly centered Gaussian, has common order \(\pi\), has mutually independent coordinate disturbance stacks, and has the positive-definite disturbance covariances (17).  By (16),
\[
\operatorname{Cov}(\widetilde X^{(a)})
=(L_\pi^{(a)})^{-1}D_\pi^{(a)}(L_\pi^{(a)})^{-\mathsf T}
=\Sigma^{aa}.
\tag{19}
\]
Thus every \(\pi\) has a full component-aligned completion of the marginal-only observable.  Conversely, at a fixed order the positive-definite marginal covariance and the population normal equations uniquely determine \(B_\pi^{(a)}\).  Therefore
\[
\Pi_{\mathrm{marg}}=\mathfrak S_V,
\qquad
\Theta_{\mathrm{marg}}=\{T_\pi:\pi\in\mathfrak S_V\}.
\tag{20}
\]

Assume again that \(\theta\notin\mathcal E_{\mathrm{all},\pi_0}\), and choose \(\pi\ne\pi_0\), possible because \(p\ge2\).  If \(T_\pi=T_{\pi_0}\), then \(L_\pi^{(a)}=L_{\pi_0}^{(a)}\) for every \(a\).  For the true order, the structural equations and component alignment give
\[
R_{\pi_0}^{ab}
=\operatorname{Cov}(\varepsilon^{(a)},\varepsilon^{(b)})
=\operatorname{diag}_{j\in V}(\Gamma_j[a,b])
\tag{21}
\]
for every pair.  Equality of residualizers would make \(R_\pi^{ab}=R_{\pi_0}^{ab}\), so (10) would give \(F_\pi^{ab}(\theta)=0\) for every \(a<b\).  This contradicts \(Q_{\mathrm{all}}(\theta)\ne0\).  Hence \(T_\pi\ne T_{\pi_0}\), and (20) implies
\[
|\Theta_{\mathrm{marg}}|\ge2.
\tag{22}
\]

If \(|C|\le1\), there is no paired cross-view block and \(\Theta_C^{\mathrm{ext}}=\Theta_{\mathrm{marg}}\ne\Theta_M(\mathcal O_M)\) by (14) and (22).  If \(|C|=2\), (12)--(14) give \(\Theta_C^{\mathrm{ext}}=\Theta_M(\mathcal O_M)=\{T_{\pi_0}\}\).  Since \(M\) is finite and \(C=M\) is feasible, the minimum exists and
\[
\kappa_{\mathrm{cal}}=2.
\tag{23}
\]
The original definition of \(S_{\min}\) minimizes over sets of size at least two, so the same argument gives \(|S_{\min}|=2\).  A two-element calibration set is proper in \(M\) exactly when \(m\ge3\).  Every step used only the defining restrictions of \(\Omega_{\pi_0}^{\mathrm{CA}}\) and \(\mathfrak M_{p,m}^{\mathrm{CA}}\); neither edge minimality nor the diversity condition of HeurtebiseEtAl2026LiMVAM was invoked.

added_lemmas.statement: Let \(G_{\mathrm{obs}}=(M,E_{\mathrm{obs}})\) be a finite undirected graph with all diagonal positions specified.  Call \(G_{\mathrm{obs}}\) completable when every real symmetric partial matrix whose principal submatrix on every clique is positive definite admits a positive-definite completion.  Then \(G_{\mathrm{obs}}\) is completable if and only if it is chordal.  Consequently, if \(G_{\mathrm{obs}}\) is chordal, \(\mathcal Q_{\pi,j}(G_{\mathrm{obs}})\) admits a positive-definite completion if and only if \(\mathcal Q_{\pi,j}(G_{\mathrm{obs}})[C,C]\succ0\) for every maximal clique \(C\) of \(G_{\mathrm{obs}}\); a completion can be produced by the sequential filling process for chordal partial matrices.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(G_{\mathrm{obs}}=(M,E_{\mathrm{obs}})\) be an arbitrary finite simple undirected view graph, let \(\mathcal O_{G_{\mathrm{obs}}}\) be as in \(\text{def:observed-view-graph-moments}\), and fix \(\pi\in\mathfrak S_V\).  There exists a full member \((P,B^0,\varepsilon,\Gamma,\pi)\in\mathfrak M_{p,m}^{\mathrm{CA}}\) whose covariance restricts to \(\mathcal O_{G_{\mathrm{obs}}}\) if and only if both of the following conditions hold:
\[
\operatorname{offdiag}(R_\pi^{ab})=0
\quad\text{for every }\{a,b\}\in E_{\mathrm{obs}},
\tag{G1}
\]
and, for every \(j\in V\), the partial matrix \(\mathcal Q_{\pi,j}(G_{\mathrm{obs}})\) admits a positive-definite completion.  In every such full completion the coefficient tuple is uniquely \(T_\pi\), and any independent choice of positive-definite completions of the matrices \(\mathcal Q_{\pi,j}(G_{\mathrm{obs}})\) supplies the full disturbance-covariance certificate.

If \(G_{\mathrm{obs}}\) is chordal, the second condition is equivalent to
\[
\mathcal Q_{\pi,j}(G_{\mathrm{obs}})[C,C]\succ0
\quad\text{for every }j\in V
\text{ and every maximal clique }C\text{ of }G_{\mathrm{obs}}.
\tag{G2}
\]
Under (G2), a constructive certificate for coordinate \(j\) is the unique optimizer
\[
\widehat\Gamma_{\pi,j}
=\operatorname*{argmax}_{K\in\mathbb S_+^m}
\left\{\det K:
K[a,a]=\mathcal Q_{\pi,j}[a,a]\ (a\in M),\ 
K[a,b]=\mathcal Q_{\pi,j}[a,b]\ (\{a,b\}\in E_{\mathrm{obs}})
\right\};
\tag{G3}
\]
this optimizer exists, is positive definite, and is unique.

Chordality cannot be omitted from the clique test.  When \(m=4\), take the chordless cycle with edges \(12,23,34,41\), put \(\Sigma^{aa}=I_p\), and on those four edges put \(\Sigma^{ab}=\rho_{ab}I_p\), where
\[
(\rho_{12},\rho_{23},\rho_{34},\rho_{41})=(0.9,0.9,0.9,-0.9).
\tag{G4}
\]
For every \(\pi\), all observed residual cross-blocks are diagonal and every specified two-by-two coordinate clique is positive definite, but no coordinate partial matrix in (G4) has even a positive-semidefinite completion.  Finally, when \(G_{\mathrm{obs}}\) is the clique on \(S\) together with isolated vertices \(M\setminus S\), this theorem reduces to \(\text{lem:fixed-order-residual-characterization}\), and the block-diagonal completion is exactly \(\Gamma_{\pi,j}\) from \(\text{def:noise-certificate}\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
We first establish two orderwise facts from \(\text{def:modified-cholesky}\).  Fix a view \(a\) and write \(P_k=\{\pi(1),\ldots,\pi(k-1)\}\).  The row indexed by \(\pi(k)\) is the unique population least-squares coefficient because \(\Sigma^{aa}[P_k,P_k]\succ0\).  Its innovation is orthogonal to the span of \(X_{P_k}^{(a)}\).  Every innovation at an earlier position belongs to that span, so distinct innovations are orthogonal.  Therefore
\[
R_\pi^{aa}=L_\pi^{(a)}\Sigma^{aa}(L_\pi^{(a)})^{\mathsf T}
\quad\text{is diagonal}.
\tag{24}
\]
The matrix \(L_\pi^{(a)}\) is unit lower triangular after ordering by \(\pi\), hence invertible.  Congruence of \(\Sigma^{aa}\succ0\) by this invertible matrix gives
\[
R_\pi^{aa}\succ0,
\qquad
R_\pi^{aa}[j,j]>0
\quad(j\in V).
\tag{25}
\]

Suppose first that a full member of \(\mathfrak M_{p,m}^{\mathrm{CA}}\) with common order \(\pi\) restricts to \(\mathcal O_{G_{\mathrm{obs}}}\).  In its equation for \(X_{\pi(k)}^{(a)}\), the disturbance \(\varepsilon_{\pi(k)}^{(a)}\) is uncorrelated with each disturbance having a different variable label by \(\text{ass:cross-variable-disturbance-orthogonality}\).  Order triangularity expresses \(X_{P_k}^{(a)}\) as a linear function of disturbances at labels in \(P_k\).  Hence
\[
\operatorname{Cov}_P\!\left(\varepsilon_{\pi(k)}^{(a)},X_{P_k}^{(a)}\right)=0.
\tag{26}
\]
For this class member, \(\Gamma_j\succ0\) gives \(\Gamma_j[a,a]>0\) for every \(j\).  The within-view disturbance covariance is therefore positive definite and diagonal, while \(I_p-B^{0,(a)}\) is unit order-triangular and invertible.  Congruence in the structural covariance formula yields \(\Sigma^{aa}\succ0\).  The normal equations and (26) consequently force its structural regression row to equal the unique row in \(B_\pi^{(a)}\).  Thus its full coefficient tuple is uniquely \(T_\pi\), and
\[
L_\pi^{(a)}X^{(a)}=\varepsilon^{(a)}.
\tag{27}
\]
For an observed edge \(\{a,b\}\), equations (27) and \(\text{ass:cross-variable-disturbance-orthogonality}\) imply
\[
R_\pi^{ab}
=\operatorname{Cov}_P(\varepsilon^{(a)},\varepsilon^{(b)})
=\operatorname{diag}_{j\in V}(\Gamma_j[a,b]),
\tag{28}
\]
which proves (G1).  For each \(j\), the full matrix \(\Gamma_j\succ0\), by \(\text{ass:disturbance-nondegeneracy}\), agrees with the diagonal and every observed edge entry of \(\mathcal Q_{\pi,j}(G_{\mathrm{obs}})\) by (27)--(28).  It is therefore the required positive-definite completion.  This proves necessity, including the asserted coefficient uniqueness.

Conversely, suppose (G1) holds and choose, independently for each \(j\in V\), a positive-definite completion \(\widetilde\Gamma_j\) of \(\mathcal Q_{\pi,j}(G_{\mathrm{obs}})\).  Let \((E_j)_{j\in V}\) be mutually independent centered Gaussian vectors in \(\mathbb R^m\) with
\[
\operatorname{Cov}(E_j)=\widetilde\Gamma_j,
\tag{29}
\]
and define \(\widetilde\varepsilon_j^{(a)}=E_j[a]\).  The coordinate stacks are mutually independent and every covariance in (29) is positive definite.  Set
\[
\widetilde X^{(a)}=(L_\pi^{(a)})^{-1}\widetilde\varepsilon^{(a)}
=(I_p-B_\pi^{(a)})^{-1}\widetilde\varepsilon^{(a)}.
\tag{30}
\]
This is a jointly centered Gaussian structural system with common order \(\pi\), cross-variable disturbance orthogonality, and disturbance nondegeneracy.

By the diagonal specifications in \(\mathcal Q_{\pi,j}\), (24), and (29),
\[
\operatorname{Cov}(\widetilde\varepsilon^{(a)})
=\operatorname{diag}_{j\in V}(\widetilde\Gamma_j[a,a])
=\operatorname{diag}_{j\in V}(R_\pi^{aa}[j,j])
=R_\pi^{aa}.
\tag{31}
\]
Consequently (30)--(31) give
\[
\operatorname{Cov}(\widetilde X^{(a)})
=(L_\pi^{(a)})^{-1}R_\pi^{aa}(L_\pi^{(a)})^{-\mathsf T}
=\Sigma^{aa}.
\tag{32}
\]
For an observed edge, the edge specifications and (G1) similarly give
\[
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Cov}(\widetilde\varepsilon^{(a)},\widetilde\varepsilon^{(b)})
&=\operatorname{diag}_{j\in V}(\widetilde\Gamma_j[a,b])\\
&=\operatorname{diag}_{j\in V}(R_\pi^{ab}[j,j])
=R_\pi^{ab}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{33}
\]
Multiplying (33) on the left by \((L_\pi^{(a)})^{-1}\) and on the right by \((L_\pi^{(b)})^{-\mathsf T}\) yields the observed \(\Sigma^{ab}\) by \(\text{def:residual-cross-blocks}\).  Thus (30) is a full member of \(\mathfrak M_{p,m}^{\mathrm{CA}}\) restricting to \(\mathcal O_{G_{\mathrm{obs}}}\).  This proves sufficiency and the assertion that the independently chosen completions are noise certificates.

Now suppose \(G_{\mathrm{obs}}\) is chordal.  A positive-definite completion necessarily has positive-definite principal submatrices on every maximal clique.  Conversely, (G2) makes the partial matrix positive definite on every clique, because each clique is contained in a maximal clique and principal submatrices of positive-definite matrices are positive definite.  The converse direction of \(\text{lem:chordal-positive-definite-completion}\) then supplies a positive-definite completion.  This proves the chordal equivalence.

For completeness, we verify the constructive max-determinant certificate (G3).  Let \(\mathcal K_j\) be its displayed feasible set.  The chordal result gives a matrix \(K_0\in\mathcal K_j\cap\mathbb S_{++}^m\), so \(\det K_0>0\).  The set \(\mathcal K_j\) is closed.  It is bounded because positive semidefiniteness and each two-by-two principal minor imply
\[
|K[a,b]|^2\le K[a,a]K[b,b]
=\mathcal Q_{\pi,j}[a,a]\mathcal Q_{\pi,j}[b,b]
\quad(a,b\in M).
\tag{34}
\]
Thus \(\mathcal K_j\) is compact, and continuity of the determinant gives a maximizer.  Its determinant is at least \(\det K_0>0\), so the maximizer is positive definite.  If distinct positive-definite matrices \(K_1,K_2\in\mathcal K_j\) both maximized the determinant, their midpoint would also be feasible and positive definite.  For every nonzero real symmetric direction \(H\), direct matrix differentiation gives
\[
D^2\log\det(K)[H,H]
=-\operatorname{tr}(K^{-1}HK^{-1}H)<0
\quad(H\ne0)
\tag{35}
\]
because the negated trace is \(-\|K^{-1/2}HK^{-1/2}\|_{\mathrm F}^2\).  Thus \(\log\det\) is strictly concave on \(\mathbb S_{++}^m\).  Applying strict concavity to \(K_1\) and \(K_2\) would make the midpoint have determinant strictly larger than their common maximum, a contradiction.  Therefore (G3) has exactly one optimizer; its positive Cholesky pivots and its equality on the displayed affine constraints give a directly checkable certificate.

We finally prove the nonchordal obstruction.  In (G4), every within-view covariance is \(I_p\), so \(\text{def:modified-cholesky}\) gives
\[
B_\pi^{(a)}=0,
\qquad L_\pi^{(a)}=I_p
\quad\text{for every }a\in M\text{ and every }\pi.
\tag{36}
\]
Hence \(R_\pi^{ab}=\rho_{ab}I_p\) on each observed edge, proving (G1).  The joint covariance of either observed edge is
\[
\begin{pmatrix}I_p&\rho_{ab}I_p\\ \rho_{ab}I_p&I_p\end{pmatrix},
\tag{37}
\]
whose eigenvalues are \(1+\rho_{ab}\) and \(1-\rho_{ab}\), each with multiplicity \(p\).  Since \(|\rho_{ab}|=0.9<1\), every observed two-view block, and in particular every specified two-by-two coordinate clique, is positive definite.

Suppose nevertheless that a coordinate partial matrix had a positive-semidefinite completion \(K\).  A Gram representation of \(K\succeq0\) gives vectors \(u_1,u_2,u_3,u_4\) with \(K[a,b]=\langle u_a,u_b\rangle\).  The unit diagonal makes \(\|u_a\|=1\).  The first three correlations in (G4) therefore imply
\[
\|u_1-u_2\|=\|u_2-u_3\|=\|u_3-u_4\|=\sqrt{2-2(0.9)}=\sqrt{0.2}.
\tag{38}
\]
The triangle inequality and (38) yield
\[
\|u_1-u_4\|\le3\sqrt{0.2},
\qquad
\langle u_1,u_4\rangle
=1-\frac12\|u_1-u_4\|^2
\ge1-\frac{1.8}{2}=0.1.
\tag{39}
\]
This contradicts the specified fourth correlation \(\langle u_1,u_4\rangle=-0.9\).  Hence no positive-semidefinite, and therefore no positive-definite, completion exists.

If \(G_{\mathrm{obs}}\) is the clique on \(S\) plus isolated vertices, its maximal cliques are \(S\) and the singleton unselected views.  For an order passing (G1), \(\text{lem:fixed-order-residual-characterization}\) proves that the selected block \((R_\pi^{ab}[j,j])_{a,b\in S}\) is positive definite, while (25) proves positivity of each isolated singleton.  The completion that sets all unspecified entries to zero is their positive-definite direct sum, exactly the matrix in \(\text{def:noise-certificate}\).  Thus the earlier selected-clique characterization is precisely this chordal special case.
added_lemmas.justification: This theorem gives the complete population feasibility test for an arbitrary graph of paired views and separates edgewise component alignment from the genuinely global positive-definite completion obstruction.
added_lemmas.gap: The selected-clique certificate in \(\text{lem:fixed-order-residual-characterization}\) is automatically completable, while GroneEtAl1984PositiveDefiniteCompletion addresses partial matrices without the LiMVAM residual reduction.  The theorem joins these ingredients and proves that nonchordal calibration graphs require more than positive edge blocks.
added_lemmas.consumer: A partially paired multi-view study can test every candidate order on its actually observed view graph, return coordinatewise max-determinant noise certificates when feasible, and detect nonchordal designs for which local edge checks are insufficient.

proposed.name: \(\mathcal O_{G_{\mathrm{obs}}}\)
proposed.construction:
Let \(G_{\mathrm{obs}}=(M,E_{\mathrm{obs}})\) be a finite simple undirected graph.  Define
\[
\mathcal O_{G_{\mathrm{obs}}}
=\left((\Sigma^{aa})_{a\in M},
(\Sigma^{ab})_{\{a,b\}\in E_{\mathrm{obs}},\,a<b}\right),
\]
where every \(\Sigma^{aa}\in\mathbb S_{++}^p\), and the opposite orientation is \(\Sigma^{ba}=(\Sigma^{ab})^{\mathsf T}\).  No cross-view block indexed by a nonedge is observed.

proposed_core_edits.reason: This definition exposes exactly which covariance blocks are available under a general graph calibration design and states the marginal positivity required by modified Cholesky inversion.

proposed.name: \(\mathcal Q_{\pi,j}(G_{\mathrm{obs}})\)
proposed.construction:
For \(\mathcal O_{G_{\mathrm{obs}}}\), a permutation \(\pi\), and \(j\in V\), define the real symmetric partial matrix \(\mathcal Q_{\pi,j}(G_{\mathrm{obs}})\) on \(M\) by
\[
\mathcal Q_{\pi,j}(G_{\mathrm{obs}})[a,a]=R_\pi^{aa}[j,j]
\quad(a\in M),
\qquad
\mathcal Q_{\pi,j}(G_{\mathrm{obs}})[a,b]
=R_\pi^{ab}[j,j]
\quad(\{a,b\}\in E_{\mathrm{obs}}),
\]
with the symmetric orientation used at \((b,a)\); entries indexed by nonedges are unspecified.  A positive-definite completion is a matrix \(K\in\mathbb S_{++}^m\) agreeing with every specified diagonal and edge entry.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The theorem's second necessary-and-sufficient condition must be a computable partial matrix with explicit specified and unspecified entries.
